newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Small plane crashes in Guatemala, no survivors.
newsitem.headline: Small plane crashes in Guatemala, no survivors.

text.p: A small private airplane crashed south of Guatemala City early on Wednesday, killing everyone on board, officials said.
"The airplane is completely destroyed and there are no survivors," Rony Paz, civil aviation chief of operations, told Reuters.
He said the plane, a Westwind 24, could carry a maximum of eight to nine people including the pilot.
Radio Sonora in Guatemala City said the plane was flying from Caracas, Venezuela, to Lima, Peru, to Guatemala City to Dallas, Texas.
The radio identified the pilot as Rafael Roman, but did not give his nationality. It said that possibly five people were on board, including an American couple.
Paz said aviation authorities would not have information on the exact number of dead until later Wednesday.
The plane went down at 3:10 a.m. (0910 GMT) south of Lake Amatitlan, 15 miles (25 km) from the capital.
